criterion_notes.c1: Examines household and community clean/drinking water service through a community-based rural piped water supply system (SPAMDes Tirto Sari Ponces) serving 125 connections (120 houses, 2 mosques, and 3 businesses) in Jambon Village, Kulon Progo Regency.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain/broad wording of Criterion 2 (plain_criterion2_decision = include) because it empirically examines community-based institutional/managerial governance of a rural water supply system, including operational management practices, monthly administrative/financial reporting, absence of written SOPs/rules and norms, and tariff-funded financial sustainability. However, it FAILS the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading (c2_legal_admin_factor = no -> exclude as E03): Government Regulation No. 122 of 2015 and Yogyakarta Governor Regulation No. 27 of 2015 are mentioned solely as unanalysed macro-governance background; the manager checklist evaluates routine technical O&M and coordination (maintenance SOPs, meetings, leak/complaint handling); and although existing customers' satisfaction with the volumetric tariff and installation fees is descriptively scored within a composite sustainability index, the study does not analyze tariff rules, eligibility rules, tenure/documentation requirements, enforcement, or regulatory/ownership rules as a mechanism governing household service access, connection, or exclusion.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary empirical data from a field infrastructure survey, structured Likert questionnaires and interviews with 3 SPAMDes managers and 21 consumer respondents, management billing/consumption records (2019-2023), and a comparative table drawing on secondary SPAMDes case studies.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports outcomes directly relevant to service access, quantity, continuity, and perceived affordability: consumer connection growth from 83 (79 houses) in 2019 to 125 (120 houses) in 2023, average demand of 371.6 L/house/day (92.9 L/person/day), lack of running water at higher-elevation houses during morning and evening peak hours, and customer satisfaction/affordability ratings for water quantity, quality, and tariffs.
criterion_notes.c5: Identifies the study design (descriptive mixed-methods case study), unit of analysis and population/sample (SPAMDes system, 3 managers, and 21 consumer households out of 125 connections in Jambon Village), operational/management dimensions assessed, and service/satisfaction outcomes, though the exposure is generic community O&M/project sustainability rather than an access-governing rule.
criterion_notes.c6: Published in English in BIO Web of Conferences.

evidence_quotes.quote: This research was focused on the Community-based Rural Water System (SPAMDes), located in Jambon Village, Kulon Progo Regency, namely the Tirto Sari Ponces Group.

This research aims to examine the characteristics of SPAMDes Tirto Sari Ponces which is located in Nanggulan sub-district, Kulon Progo Regency starting from management, services and network infrastructure conditions.

From these factors, the aspects reviewed through the questionnaire include operational system, regular meeting between managers, regular meeting with customers, water quality, water quantity, service, information, and tariff.

Based on the results of the questionnaire, the operational system implemented at SPAMDes Tirto Ponces is relatively conventional and not comprehensive. Written SOPs regarding operational systems have not been established.

This research was conducted through field surveys, questionnaires and interviews. The field survey was to determine the condition of the SPAMDes network infrastructure. Meanwhile, questionnaires are used to obtain the required qualitative data.

However, during peak user hours, such as in the morning and evening before Maghrib prayers, there are residents' houses that do not have running water. This is because the residents' houses are located in higher areas.

The standard water tariff depends on the amount of water used. The price for using is IDR 2,500/m3, while the operational costs is IDR 3,000. Installation fees for new users which is about IDR 600,000 (own area) and IDR. 700,000 (outside the region) deemed as an affordable price and in line with market prices.

raw_response.exposure: Community-based rural water supply (SPAMDes) operational management and sustainability characteristics (infrastructure maintenance, manager meetings and monthly financial/administrative reporting, complaint handling, communication channels, and tariff-based cost recovery)
raw_response.outcome: Connected consumer counts (83 in 2019 to 125 in 2023), average household water consumption (371.6 L/house/day or 92.9 L/person/day), peak-hour flow continuity (intermittency at higher-elevation homes), customer Likert satisfaction with water quality, quantity, serviceability, and tariff/installation-fee affordability, and composite sustainability scores
raw_response.population_and_sample: SPAMDes Tirto Sari Ponces community-based rural water system in Jambon Village, Nanggulan Sub-district, Kulon Progo Regency, Yogyakarta Province, Indonesia (serving 125 connections in 2023: 120 houses, 2 mosques, and 3 businesses); empirical sample of 3 SPAMDes managers and 21 consumer respondents
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure) per the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification. Although the study empirically examines a community-managed rural water supply system (SPAMDes Tirto Sari Ponces) and reports household connection counts, consumption, peak-hour continuity, and user satisfaction/affordability (satisfying c1, c3, c4, c5, and c6, as well as the plain broad wording of Criterion 2), its focus is a descriptive civil-engineering and operational sustainability/customer-satisfaction evaluation of generic community water project management rather than a rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism directly governing service access. Statutory references (Government Regulation No. 122/2015) are unanalysed background, peak-hour supply gaps are attributed to elevation hydraulics, and tariff/installation-fee satisfaction is descriptively summarized among 21 already-connected customers without analyzing tariff, eligibility, or institutional rules as mechanisms governing access or exclusion.
raw_response.study_design: Cross-sectional descriptive mixed-methods case study (field infrastructure inspection, structured Likert questionnaires, interviews, administrative billing records, and secondary literature comparison)
